stem: Meera starts facing north. She turns 90 degrees clockwise, then walks 8 m. She then turns 90 degrees anticlockwise and walks 6 m. She finally turns 180 degrees. In which direction is she now facing?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student treats the final 180 degrees turn as a 90 degrees left turn from North, arriving at West instead of South.
Student skips the final 180 degrees turn and reports the direction after the first clockwise turn, giving East.
Student skips the final 180 degrees turn entirely, reporting North after the second segment.
Start N, CW 90 degrees -> E, walk 8 m. ACW 90 degrees from E -> N, walk 6 m. 180 degrees from N -> S. Final direction: South.

explanation: Start facing North. CW 90: East. Walk 8 m (direction unchanged). ACW 90 from East: North. Walk 6 m (direction unchanged). 180 from North: South. Final facing: South.

explanation_sections.punchline: Lock the first turn: CW 90 from North gives East. That is the cracking move because it anchors every subsequent facing. The final 180 from North returns South.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply turns in left-to-right order, most certain first. Step 1 (fixed start): North. Step 2 (CW 90): East. Step 3 (ACW 90 from East): North. Step 4 (180 from North): South. Distance walked at each step is irrelevant to facing direction - ignore it. Verify: did you apply all three turns? Yes. Final facing: South. This recipe works for any chained-turn direction problem: write each heading before reading the next turn.
explanation_sections.lesson: A CW 90 followed by an ACW 90 is a net zero rotation - you return to your original heading. A 180 always gives the exact opposite direction. Use these shortcuts to sanity-check your chain.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60 seconds. Each turn resolves in under 10 seconds. Three turns total. The trap is skipping the last 180 turn and reporting North (option 2) - always count how many turns are in the stem before you start.
